title: Before and After the Descent
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def walk(n, label):
    if n == 0:
        print(label, "base")
        return 1
    print(label, "enter", n)
    result = walk(n - 1, label)
    if n % 2 == 0:
        print(label, "exit", n, result)
    return result + n
start = 3
answer = walk(start, "A")
print("answer", answer)
expected_stdout:
A enter 3
A enter 2
A enter 1
A base
A exit 2 2
answer 7
explanation: Entry prints occur before descending 3→2→1→0. The even-frame exit prints while unwinding from n=2, when the recursive result is 2.

title: Two Recursive Branches
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def choices(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return n + 1
    left = choices(n - 1)
    print("left", n, left)
    right = choices(n - 2)
    total = left + right
    if n == 3:
        print("merge", n, total)
    return total
value = choices(3)
print("final", value)
explanation: The left subtree is evaluated fully before the right subtree. The merge print occurs after both branches return.

title: Recursive String Unwinding
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def peel(word):
    if len(word) == 1:
        print("middle", word)
        return word
    first = word[0]
    print("before", first)
    tail = peel(word[1:])
    if first in "aeiou":
        print("after", first)
    return tail + first
result = peel("team")
print("result", result)
expected_stdout:
before t
before e
before a
middle m
after a
after e
result maet
explanation: The before prints trace the call descent. The vowel after prints occur in reverse order while unwinding the stack.

title: Odd-Only Exit Prints
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def build(n, total):
    if n < 1:
        return total
    print("in", n, total)
    updated = total + n
    result = build(n - 2, updated)
    if n % 2:
        print("out", n, result)
    return result + 1
number = 5
value = build(number, 0)
print("value", value)
expected_stdout:
in 5 0
in 3 5
in 1 8
out 1 9
out 3 10
out 5 11
value 12
explanation: Calls go 5→3→1→-1. All exit prints happen after recursion, when the carried result is returned and incremented by each frame.

title: Downward and Upward Counters
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def bounce(n, counter):
    if n == 0:
        print("base", counter[0])
        return counter[0]
    counter[0] += n
    if n > 1:
        print("down", n, counter[0])
    result = bounce(n - 1, counter)
    counter[0] -= 1
    print("up", n, counter[0])
    return result + n
state = [0]
print("result", bounce(3, state))
expected_stdout:
down 3 3
down 2 5
base 6
up 1 5
up 2 4
up 3 3
result 12
explanation: The shared counter rises during descent. Base sees six; each returning frame decrements it before the up print.

title: Recursive Digit Reduction
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def reduce_digits(n):
    if n < 10:
        return n
    last = n % 10
    rest = n // 10
    print("take", last)
    reduced = reduce_digits(rest)
    if last % 2 == 0:
        print("even", last, reduced)
    return reduced + last
value = reduce_digits(246)
print("total", value)
explanation: Digits are taken from right to left. The even prints wait until recursive calls return from the leading digit.

title: Recursive List Segments
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def split_sum(items, start, end):
    if end - start == 1:
        return items[start]
    middle = (start + end) // 2
    left = split_sum(items, start, middle)
    right = split_sum(items, middle, end)
    print("merge", start, end, left + right)
    return left + right
numbers = [2, 1, 3, 4]
answer = split_sum(numbers, 0, len(numbers))
print("answer", answer)
explanation: Leaf calls return without printing; each merge print happens after both halves have returned, left subtree before right subtree.

title: Return Values Choose the Print
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def sequence(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return [0]
    prefix = sequence(n - 1)
    current = prefix[-1] + n
    result = prefix + [current]
    if n in (1, 3):
        print("step", n, result[-2:])
    return result
created = sequence(4)
print("last", created[-1])
print("len", len(created))
explanation: Every frame waits for the smaller prefix to return. Only frames n=1 and n=3 print their last two elements on unwinding.

title: Alternating Recursive Path
instructions: Track recursive calls and determine which prints occur on entry and which occur during return. Enter exact stdout.
code:
def trace(n, flag):
    if n == 0:
        return "X"
    print("enter", n, flag)
    next_flag = not flag
    tail = trace(n - 1, next_flag)
    if flag:
        print("return", n, tail)
        return tail + "A"
    return tail + "B"
output = trace(3, True)
print("path", output)
expected_stdout:
enter 3 True
enter 2 False
enter 1 True
return 1 X
return 3 XAB
path XABA
explanation: Flags alternate during descent. Only true-flag frames print on the way back, with the lower frame's returned string available first.
